Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
27-year-old male with 3-day history of profuse watery diarrhoea (hourly), crampy mid-lower abdominal pain (~6/10), occasional vomiting (worse with milk), subjective fever, and reduced urine frequency. Brother has similar illness, supporting infectious etiology. No blood in stool, no red-flag weight loss. Family history notable for father with colon cancer.

Most likely diagnosis: acute infectious gastroenteritis (viral > bacterial). Transient post-infectious lactose intolerance may be contributing to milk-triggered vomiting.

Plan:
• Oral rehydration therapy: purchase over-the-counter Dioralyte; advise liberal clear fluids.  
• Diet: soft/bland foods (soup, mashed foods); avoid dairy until recovery; re-introduce solids gradually.  
• Symptomatic relief: paracetamol for pain/fever.  
• Avoid alcohol; minimize smoking.  
• Safety-net: return / phone review within 48 hrs if symptoms not improving, if unable to keep fluids down, signs of dehydration (dizziness, very low urine output), bloody stools, or high fever.  
• Potential further work-up (stool cultures, blood tests, IV fluids) if no improvement.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Acute viral gastroenteritis (High) – abrupt onset, watery stool, sibling affected, self-limiting course.  
2. Acute bacterial gastroenteritis / food-borne infection (Moderate) – similar presentation; frequent takeaway food; subjective fever.  
3. Transient post-infective lactose intolerance (Low–Moderate) – vomiting triggered by milk; can follow enteric infection.
